The aromatic protons are likely part of a benzene ring, while the aliphatic protons suggest a more complex aliphatic structure, possibly with branching or multiple substituents. The coupling patterns and multiplicities provide further clues about the connectivity and environment of these protons. To narrow down the possible structures, I should now determine the molecular formula using mass spectrometry, which will help in identifying the exact number of atoms present.</thought>

With this information, I can now deduce the molecular formula. Given the presence of aromatic and aliphatic components, a likely candidate could be C14H18, which matches the observed mass and the NMR data. To confirm this, I will generate the chemical formula from the SMILES string and check for consistency.</thought>
